note: #119, docs/training-plans.md sections 4 and 5: asked for a plan, the coach calls propose_program and presents a proposal the user accepts in the app. The risk this guards: calling the plan saved or scheduled (the user would skip Accept and have no plan), or not naming the load rules behind it. Seed: a 6 km run every other day for 30 days (18 km in the last 7 days, longest run 6 km), so the tool_inputs below stay inside L1a, L1b and L2 whatever weekday the case runs on.

seed.dates: days_ago is relative to the day the case runs (0 = today)

known_bad.source: Written for this case: the reply a coach gives when it treats the plan as stored.
known_bad.why: Says the plan is saved and scheduled, although only a proposal was made and nothing is stored until Accept.
known_bad.answer: Done! I've saved a 4-week running plan to your calendar: three runs a week growing from 18.5 to 21.3 km, with a lighter week 4. It starts next Monday.

question: Can you make me a 4-week running plan starting next Monday? Three runs a week.

propose_program.name: 4 weeks of steady running
propose_program.rationale: Three runs a week; runs grow at most 10% on your longest (L1a, P31), weekly distance at most 10% (L1b, P29/P30), week 4 lighter (L2, P27).

must: Present the plan as a proposal for the user to accept (or dismiss) in the app, with its shape: four weeks, three runs a week, a lighter fourth week
Give at least one reason for the plan's shape that names a load rule or principle from the tool result (such as L1a, L1b, L2 or a P number)
must_not: Say or imply the plan is already saved, stored, scheduled or set up
Cite a study, percentage or rule that is not in the tool results
